newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Western advertisers seek Eastern European markets.
newsitem.headline: Western advertisers seek Eastern European markets.

text.p: Western advertisers seeking new consumer markets in the former Soviet bloc urged East European countries on Wednesday to adopt liberal self-regulation of their emerging advertising industries.
The message went out to advertisers, manufacturers and government officials from Eastern and Western Europe attending a one-day conference in Prague on advertising and self-regulation.
"We consider self-regulation within a legal framework to be the best method of maintaining high industry standards and ensuring consumer confidence," Christopher Ogden told the conference.

Ogden, chairman of the European Advertising Standards Alliance (EASA), told delegates Eastern Europe should copy self-regulatory advertising frameworks that he said already worked well in several Western European countries.

Western manufacturers who make everything from shampoo to cars to tobacco products are struggling with growing competition in their traditional markets and are aggressively searching for new consumer turf.
Advertisers hope Eastern Europe will offer a double bonus: shoppers keen to buy Western goods and a lack of restrictions that limit promotion of goods like tobacco and alcohol products in the West.
A number of consumer groups in Western Europe want to see tighter controls on things like advertising tobacco and alcohol, and targetting children with advertising.

But Ogden, who is also deputy director general of Britain's Advertising Standards Authority, the self-regulatory body that oversees non-broadcast advertising, said self-regulation worked well in Western European and was more efficient than government control.
The conference, called "West Goes East", included speakers from companies that made alcoholic beverages, non-prescription medicines, cosmetics, tobacco and food.
The conference was organised by the Czech Republic's self-regulating advertising group, Rada Pro Reklamu.

With the fall of communism and the development of market economies, the advertising industry has grown rapidly in Central and Eastern Europe, with tobacco companies and consumer products manufacturers among the most aggressive advertisers.
Ogden said the advertising industry had to maintain a high degree of responsibility if self-regulation -- which is basically paid for by the industry in Western Europe --were to succeed.

"Self-regulation is just that, and if there is to be no cost to the state or the individual consumer in the operation of the system then the industry must demonstrate its commitment by paying what is required," he said.

The EASA, whose 21 member countries include Eastern European nations such as the Slovak Republic and Slovenia as well as members of the European Union, aims to support and promote self-regulation and coordinate cross-border complaints.

Within the Czech Republic Ogden said there were two main challenges for self-regulation: companies there were becoming increasingly sophisticated in selling things and consumers were more and more aware of choice and their rights.
